explanations: There is none. Malformed payloads (InvalidReadingError) go straight to the DLQ instead of burning retries; transient failures are republished with an incremented x-attempts until MAX_ATTEMPTS, then dead-lettered. The original is acked only after the retry or DLQ publish is confirmed by the broker, so a crash or publish failure leaves the message on the queue (nack with requeue) rather than losing it. The dead-lettered copy keeps the payload, message id, original headers, and adds the reason, attempt count, origin queue, and timestamp needed to inspect or replay it.

parseReading throws InvalidReadingError when typeof value is not number, and handle sends any InvalidReadingError directly to deadLetter regardless of attempts. No retry is scheduled, it is acked after the DLQ publish rather than requeued, and there is no coercion.

attempts is 2, below MAX_ATTEMPTS, so scheduleRetry publishes with x-attempts attempts + 1 = 3 and delay min(60000, 1000 * 2^(2-1)) = 2000 ms, then acks the original. The DLQ is used only at 5 attempts or for invalid payloads, and nack-requeue is only the fallback when the reroute publish itself fails.

publishConfirmed rejects when the broker does not confirm, the inner catch logs and calls nack(msg, false, true), and the original stays available for redelivery. ack runs only after a successful publish, the inner catch prevents the rejection from escaping the void-ed promise, and there is no fallback to the retry exchange.
